best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Spectro DMG% boost, a 20% CRIT RATE buff for 15 seconds after inflicting Spectro Frazzle and further 15% Spectro DMG% boost for 15 seconds after attacking an enemy that has 10 Spectro Frazzle stacks. For characters that have the capability to inflict Spectro Frazzle in their kit the 20% CRIT RATE is all but permanant, while the 15% Spectro DMG boost should maintain decent uptime in Spectro Frazzle focused teams. Generally the best in slot set for all characters capable of inflicting Spectro Frazzle. When playing Phoebe in Absolution, she will require the assistance of her team in order to activate the 15% Spectro DMG boost tied to hitting enemies with at least 10 stacks of Spectro Frazzle - as in this state she cannot achieve that herself.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Gives 12% Spectro DMG Bonus when equipped in the Main Slot. Trades off character buffing for personal damage from the Echo Skill cast itself, since it deals higher damage to enemies inflicted with Spectro Frazzle. Overall a super negligible difference from Capitaneus though.

Gives 12% Spectro and 12% Heavy DMG Bonus when equipped in the Main Slot. Trades off damage from the Echo Skill cast for character buffing which makes it slightly stronger in most teams except Lynae where Liberation damage takes more of Phoebe's damage total.

best_echo_sets.commentary: This set sacrifices Phoebe's personal damage in order to provide higher buffing to a single character, making it the best set for Hybrid Phoebe as a Zani buffer. It provides an extra 10% Energy Regen to the wielder unconditionally and gives 22.5% ATK to the incoming character for 15s after casting Outro skill.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: The best and only real option 5P Moonlit Clouds has, as it grants an extra 12% DMG Bonus on top of the ATK boost to the next character that Moonlit Clouds would usually give. Additionally restores a lot of Energy to the caster when it deals damage, though this won't really see use on Phoebe since it will be usually cancelled by her Outro.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Phoebe's signature weapon gives her a ton of CRIT Rate, ATK%, Heavy and Basic DMG bonus under the condition that the enemy is affected by Spectro Frazzle - it even amplifies Spectro Frazzle DMG after an Outro. All of these perks make this weapon the best for Phoebe both as a DPS and a Support.

Spectro Rover is the strongest partner by far if played in Quickswap. The majority of players should however stick to Shorekeeper for the easiest experience.
Only use this team if you have a lot of quickswap experience, else consider other teams. Ciaccona is only worth using for Whimpering Wastes.
Spectro Rover should be on Moonlit Clouds.

cons: In Absolution Mode, needs a teammate who applies Spectro Frazzle which restricts teambuilding, and is not suited to multiwave content due to the lack of multiwave Spectro Frazzle appliers — additionally benefits very little from Outro buffs due to her Heavy Attacks already gaining massive DMG Amplify bonuses;
In Confession mode, deals rather subpar damage and is reliant on Spectro Frazzle Main DPS characters to deal damage (only Zani currently).
pros: Can be played both as a DPS (Absolution) and a Hybrid (Confession) by choosing between two different modes when fighting;
In Absolution mode, has wide AoE attacks that deal potent, straightforward, easily exploitable damage with consistent output. Additionally has very F2P-friendly team options;
In Confession mode, has a medium-short rotation with huge Spectro Frazzle-related buffs;
Arguably the most F2P-friendly character in the game, functioning very effectively as the only limited 5-star character on the team with effective F2P-accessible builds and weapon options.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Phoebe is a 5-star Spectro Rectifier DPS and Hybrid character who relies upon or applies Spectro Frazzle in order to deal damage or enable/boost the damage of teammates. She's characterized by her two different modes allowing for two different playstyles: "Absolution" and "Confession". In Absolution mode, Phoebe acts as the Main DPS of the team, able to dish out lots of damage on her own as long as Spectro Frazzle is applied on enemies. In Confession mode, Phoebe is instead a secondary character much like Sanhua or Mortefi who will amplify the Spectro Frazzle DMG of other characters on your team. She also applies the most Spectro Frazzle of any character in the game, and can reduce the Spectro RES of enemies to further increase Spectro damage of your Main DPS. Generally speaking, her attacks feature good AoE and even grouping, making her suited to handling several enemies at once if required.

Accessing either Absolution or Confession state is done via consuming one of her Forte bars called "Prayer". Entering either state gives Phoebe 12% Spectro DMG Bonus. 120 Prayer which restores in 24 seconds total at a rate of 5 per second - all of Phoebe's rotations will operate on this cooldown. Absolution is entered via casting a Heavy Attack with full Prayer, called "Absolution Litany". Confession is entered via holding down Resonance Skill with full Prayer which performs a Resonance Skill called "Utter Confession". Casting either of these attacks restore Phoebe's second Forte bar, called "Divine Voice" which she restores the full 60 points of. These points will be consumed to cast her special Heavy Attacks, called "Starflash", which can only be executed after Basic Attack 3 or a Dodge Counter, and have different effects depending on Phoebe's state:
In Absolution mode, Phoebe deals gains 256% Heavy ATK DMG Amplify on Starflash and they consume 15 Divine Voice (4 per rotation);
In Confession mode, Phoebe applies 5 stacks of Spectro Frazzle to any enemies hit by Starflash and they consume 30 Divine Voice (2 per rotation).

Phoebe's regular Basic Attacks can be ignored, however they get enhanced once her base Resonance Skill is activated: it summons a special zone called "Ring of Mirrors" at the skill's target location for 30 seconds. Summoning this ring freezes any targets hit in place for 2 seconds, and allows her to cast her Resonance Skill again shortly after to teleport in its center. While standing outside of this Ring of Mirrors, her Basic Attacks will group enemies in its center along with a small extra attack. While standing inside of it, her Basic Attacks deal much more significant damage, roughly double the typical amount. This is unchanged whether Phoebe is in Absolution or Confession mode.

Other abilities affected by whether Phoebe is in Absolution or Confession include her Ultimate, which has a 255% multiplier increase in Absolution and applies 8 stacks of Spectro Frazzle to targets hit in Confession. Lastly, her Outro also gets a 255% multiplier increase in Absolution mode, and in Confession mode it gives the on-field character an effect called "Silent Prayer" for 30s, during which the Spectro RES of nearby targets is reduced by 10% and the character gets 100% Spectro Frazzle DMG Amplify.

With all of this explained, we can conclude that typically Phoebe's rotation will have you execute her Resonance Skill to summon the Ring of Mirrors, then enter either state depending on your team before casting your Ultimate (you can also cancel the animation of Absolution Litany or Utter Confession using this Ultimate for lower field time), after which you should enter the Ring of Mirrors to either do 3 Basic Attacks then Starflash, or a Dodge Counter then Starflash a total of 2 to 4 times depending on your state. After all of these actions are performed, Phoebe is ready to cast her Outro to either deal the rest of her damage or apply all of her buffs.

It should be easy to tell by the fact that Phoebe has 2 completely different modes of operation that she's a very flexible character. You'd be correct to assume this — however Phoebe does have the restriction of being tied to Spectro Frazzle team compositions, whether that's because she buffs that type of damage or because she relies on Spectro Frazzle to deal damage. But beyond that restriction, Phoebe slots in any Spectro Frazzle team very well, whether that's as a Spectro Frazzle Main DPS or a Hybrid Spectro Frazzle buffer. Generally speaking, Phoebe has lots of teammates to work with featuring two different playstyles, so feel free to play whatever's most comfortable or available for you.

Phoebe has a few weaknesses to take note of, beyond being simply tied to Spectro Frazzle. In Absolution mode, she needs Spectro Frazzle to be present on the enemies themselves — you'd be correct to assume you need to re-apply Spectro Frazzle to any new enemies than spawn in, otherwise Phoebe will deal very little damage (as her Starflash damage will be equivalent to her Confession state). This causes problems in content such as Whimpering Wastes. In Confession Mode, her team options are very scarce; right now she's exclusively tied to Zani, as that is the only Main DPS who can take advantage of Confession Phoebe's Spectro Frazzle buffs.

Outside of that however, Phoebe is first of all a very potent, flexible character who's able to act both as a potent Main DPS with high and consistent damage output, but also as a buffer to Spectro Frazzle damage if you own a character who benefits from that (only Zani currently). This gives her a lot of value as even though her Confession Hybrid teams are very restrictive, her Absolution DPS team compositions are flexible and F2P-friendly, as they function just fine with a character like Spectro Rover to take her damage as high as can be.

In conclusion, Phoebe is a character who's not only able to act as two different roles, filling two different meta niches and having two different playstyles, but she's also able to act very effectively at both of these roles. Overall, Phoebe can be exploited well by every player, and yield good results as her performance in either Absolution or Confession mode is felt on every team she's functional in. This gives her a very unique but also solid presence in the Wuthering Waves meta.

She's characterized by her two different modes allowing for two different playstyles: "Absolution" and "Confession". In Absolution mode, Phoebe acts as the Main DPS of the team, able to dish out lots of damage on her own as long as Spectro Frazzle is applied on enemies. In Confession mode, Phoebe is instead a secondary character much like Sanhua or Mortefi who will amplify the Spectro Frazzle DMG of other characters on your team. She also applies the most Spectro Frazzle of any character in the game, and can reduce the Spectro RES of enemies to further increase Spectro damage of your Main DPS. steps: The first optimization is to implement Dash Cancels during Chamuel's Star P3 in order to cancel the end lag that comes with the ability. Doing this doesn't cost Phoebe any damage and will allow her to get to her next ability faster.
The second optimization is to implement Swap Cancels during Phoebe's Star Flash Heavy Attacks. This allows you to weave in the abilities of other resonators without costing Phoebe any field time.

The third optimization is to use Phoebe's ultimate to cancel the animation of Absolution Litany right after you use it. Doing this will retain all the damage and effects of both ability but save significant time.
The rotation above remains the same but here are all the places you can implement the above optimizations to save time:

synergies.commentary: As Confession Phoebe's only synergy currently, Zani's damage output is buffed to tremendous heights as she mostly deals Spectro Frazzle DMG during her Ultimate stance. Providing Spectro RES Shred and massive Spectro Frazzle DMG Amplify boosts on Outro, Phoebe is by far and away the best option for Zani, making for one of the top teams in the meta.

These are Phoebe's main Negative Status appliers. Phoebe needs Spectro Frazzle to function as a DPS, Spectro Rover is the character of choice in single-wave while Ciaccona will be preferred in multi-wave. Finally, Chisa is great as a quickswap support/secondary damage dealer option who can buff Phoebe well with her Outro, Rejuvenating Glow and her Weapon while also dealing good damage of her own if her swap windows are properly utilized.

The best second slot partners for DPS Phoebe by far, Lynae provides the strongest generalist buffs which make her stand above every other buffing option for Phoebe and makes for her best team; Rebecca is a very close contender as she can provide a ramp-up Heavy DMG buff, several generalist buffs, and her own personal damage. Phrolova is a more damage-oriented version of this with lower buffs, since she can provide Heavy ATK DMG Amplification via her Outro but most importantly a ton of personal damage and crowd control at relatively low field time costs for a DPS (but still a higher field time compared to the previous two).

Additional buffing options for Phoebe. Mortefi and Iuno provide Heavy ATK DMG Amplification and some personal damage, but while it is Phoebe's main damage type, the Amplification stat is already too saturated on her because of her kit and as a result the buff has minimal value; Sanhua hence presents herself as another fully F2P-accessible option which buffs Basic Attacks via her Outro instead, which winds up to be equivalent to Mortefi's buffing profile, with Iuno providing less buffs and having higher personal damagee instead.
